                       Bidirectional Latent Planning

The robust execution of long-horizon manipulation tasks re-             ecution has become the prevailing paradigm [5, 10, 14].
mains a central challenge in embodied intelligence, neces-              However, achieving robust long-horizon manipulation re-
sitating both coherent high-level planning and reliable low-            quires solving two fundamental and distinct challenges si-
level control. Existing approaches often encounter two crit-            multaneously. The first challenge is temporal robustness:
ical limitations: the accumulation of prediction errors in              the ability to generate a plan that remains coherent and dy-
subgoal planning, leading to compounding deviations over                namically consistent over an extended time horizon. The
time; and the planning-execution gap, where high-level ab-              second, complementary challenge is spatial robustness: the
stract plans fail to be effectively grounded in the continuous          ability to reliably ground an abstract, high-level plan into
perception-action space. To address these challenges, we                the noisy, high-dimensional perception-action space at the
propose a novel unified framework, Affordance-Grounded                  moment of execution.
Bidirectional Latent Planning (AGiLe). AGiLe introduces                    Existing robotic planning approaches often fail to ad-
a bidirectional latent planning mechanism that jointly opti-            dress both requirements simultaneously. Approaches that
mizes a backward planner and a forward critic. The back-                operate at a fine-grained granularity, such as dense video
ward planner generates goal-directed subgoals from the fi-              prediction models like Seer [37], provide detailed guid-
nal objective, while the forward critic assesses their reacha-          ance but suffer from prohibitive computational costs [2, 11,
bility, ensuring temporal robustness through sustained con-             18]. In contrast, coarse-grained forward-predictive meth-
sistency in long-horizon planning. Furthermore, AGiLe                   ods, which plan in larger steps, are often prone to failing
bridges the planning-execution gap by leveraging affor-                 in terms of temporal robustness [4]. These methods accu-
dance as structural guidance, grounding abstract subgoals               mulate errors over time, where small, early deviations in
into dense, pixel-level visual affordances that drive action.           predictions compound and cause the plan to diverge from
This enhances spatial robustness, enabling the system to                the intended goal. Recently, Liu et al. proposed a Latent
effectively adapt to semantic and visual distractors. Ex-               Backward Planning (LBP) scheme to better address this
tensive empirical evaluations across both simulation and                temporal challenge by reasoning in reverse order. How-
real-world settings confirm that AGiLe significantly out-               ever, while LBP improves temporal consistency, its unidi-
performs strong baselines, achieving an 8.5% improve-                   rectional nature only partially resolves the temporal issue,
ment over prior state-of-the-art methods and demonstrating              as it may generate plans that are inconsistent with or infea-
strong effectiveness and robustness in long-horizon manip-              sible from the current state. More critically, LBP does not
ulation tasks. Project website: https://agile-long.github.io.           explicitly tackle the challenge of spatial robustness. This
                                                                        planning-execution gap persists even when the plan is tem-
                                                                        porally sound. For instance, in a task like “put both moka

general-purpose robotic intelligence. This requires long-               of spatial, not temporal, robustness, underscoring the need
horizon manipulation capability—the ability to coherently               for effective perceptual grounding.

Figure 2. The Overview of AGiLe Framework. (1) Bidirectional Latent Planning: A pre-trained DecisionNCE encodes the initial
observation to z0 and language instruction to zg . The Backward Planner generates a subgoal sequence (Zplan ), which the Forward Critic
validates for feasibility. (2) Affordance Grounding and Policy Learning: The latent subgoal plan, fused with z0 , forms a task-specific
Query. This Query interacts with current visual features (from a Visual Encoder) via a Cross-Modal Grounding Module, yielding a
grounded feature. This grounded feature, combined with the robot’s proprioceptive state, conditions a Conditional Denoising Diffusion
Probabilistic Model to generate precise low-level actions for task execution.

to do it” (affordance-grounded execution), significantly en-
hancing robustness in long-horizon manipulation.

Simulation Benchmark Our primary simulation testbed                         the LIBERO-LONG benchmark, our comparison suite in-
is the LIBERO-LONG benchmark [26], specifically de-                         cludes several prominent paradigms, such as the multi-
signed for evaluating long-horizon manipulation. This                       task imitation learning policy MTACT [50], large-scale
suite comprises 10 distinct tasks that require multi-stage                  pre-trained models like MVP [45] and OpenVLA [21],
decision-making and the integration of various skills, such                 the interaction-oriented method MPI [48], and forward-
as object manipulation, stove operation, and microwave                      predictive planners like SuSIE [4] and Seer [37]. A key
closing. The complexity and diversity of these scenarios                    baseline for our work is LBP [27], a recent robotic planning
make it a robust platform for assessing planning capabil-                   SOTA method that generates subgoals in reverse temporal
ities. Adhering to the benchmark’s standard protocol, all                   order. LBP reasons backward from the final goal to the
models are trained using a fixed set of 50 expert demon-                    current state, a coarse-to-fine strategy designed to improve
strations for each task. Further details regarding the sim-                 long-horizon consistency and mitigate the compounding er-
ulation tasks can be found in Appendix B.1. Additionally,                   rors common in forward-only prediction. Given its strong
Appendix B.2 includes further experimental results, encom-                  performance in simulation and its conceptual relevance to
passing our qualitative analysis of affordance as well as a                 our bidirectional approach, we select LBP as our primary
failure case analysis.                                                      SOTA comparison for the real-world experiments.

       In conclusion, the two components play complementary
   roles: the bidirectional planner maintains temporal robust-                                                        In this paper, we present Affordance-Grounded
   ness by generating logically coherent and goal-consistent                                                          Bidirectional Latent Planning (AGiLe), a framework
   subgoal sequences, while the affordance grounding mod-                                                             for robust, language-guided, long-horizon robotic ma-
   ule ensures spatial robustness by grounding abstract sub-                                                          nipulation. AGiLe integrates two key modules to ensure
   goals into executable actions. Together, they enable AG-                                                           both temporal and spatial robustness: a bidirectional latent
   iLe’s superior performance in long-horizon manipulation                                                            planning module that maintains temporal consistency by
   tasks. More ablation studies can be found in Appendix B.4.                                                         generating logically coherent and goal-consistent subgoal
                                                                                                                      plans across long horizons, and an affordance grounding
   5.4. Real-World Validation                                                                                         module that enhances spatial robustness by dynamically
   To address RQ3 and verify that AGiLe’s architectural ad-                                                           grounding these abstract plans to task-relevant visual
   vantages translate into robust real-world execution, we eval-                                                      features, thereby effectively bridging the perception–action
   uate it on four challenging physical manipulation tasks.                                                           gap. Extensive experiments show that AGiLe achieves
   AGiLe, trained on 100 expert demonstrations for 4-stage                                                            state-of-the-art performance on simulated long-horizon ma-
   tasks and 150 for 6-stage tasks, is directly compared with                                                         nipulation benchmarks and demonstrates strong robustness
   the LBP baseline trained on the same datasets.                                                                     in real-world long-horizon manipulation tasks.
